public_rationale: Marcus predicted that no single system would solve more than 4 of the 10 Marcus–Brundage tasks by the end of 2025. An independent year-end review graded this correct: AI could perhaps pass the reading comprehension task, but could not do any four. A prediction market on the claim resolved NO (the prediction held), though it relied on Marcus's own appraisal. Game-learning results in 2026 also suggest that task was unmet. No source shows any system doing five or more.
limitations: There is no official judging-panel score; this rests on one independent review plus context.
Several tasks call for quality judgments.

our_interpretation: The tasks are the ten listed in the Marcus–Brundage bet (for example: understanding films and novels, writing obituaries without hallucinations, learning video games, writing legal briefs, writing 10,000 lines of bug-free code, prize-calibre books, screenplays and discoveries, and formalizing proofs).
Supported if no single system credibly did five or more by 31 December 2025.
criteria.support_condition: Independent assessments at the end of 2025 find that no single system performed five or more of the tasks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evidence that one system performed at least five of the tasks by end of 2025.
